article.headline: Scores from last Night: St. Andrew’s sweeps Northeast Jones; Canton edges Grenada
article.html:
St. Andrew’s Episcopal left Laurel with two soccer wins and two unbeaten records intact on Monday, November 2. The boys defeated Northeast Jones 5–0 and the girls won 1–0, moving both Saints teams to 3–0.

Canton’s boys supplied another notable road result, edging Grenada 3–2 for their first win in the reported season record. The Canton–Grenada and St. Andrew’s–Northeast Jones boys matches were featured in our Monday Games To Watch preview.

St. Andrew’s wins both without conceding

The Saints’ boys continued a defensive start that has yet to yield a goal. Their 5–0 victory brought the reported season totals to 14 goals scored and none allowed. St. Andrew’s has now won all three of its opening matches.

The girls needed a much narrower margin, but their 1–0 win produced the same outcome: another road victory and a 3–0 record. Northeast Jones finished the match scoreless, giving St. Andrew’s clean sheets in both meetings.

Canton boys edge Grenada; Chargers girls win

Canton’s 3–2 boys victory moved the Tigers to 1–1 and left Grenada at 2–3. The one-goal result gave Canton its first reported win after opening the season with a loss.

Grenada’s girls kept Canton off the board in a 7–0 home win. The Chargers improved to 2–2–1, giving Grenada a split of the two varsity results against Canton.

Pisgah and Laurel sweep soccer pairs

Pisgah won both matches at Loyd Star. The boys won the higher-scoring match 5–3, while the girls earned a 5–0 shutout.

Laurel also won both at home against North Forrest, taking the boys match 4–2 and the girls match 8–2. The girls scored four times in each half, while North Forrest scored once on either side of halftime.

Booneville and South Pontotoc trade shutouts

The same final score produced opposite winners at South Pontotoc. Booneville’s boys won 5–0, scoring twice before halftime and three times afterward. South Pontotoc’s girls reversed that result with a 5–0 win, building their score with three first-half goals and two in the second half.

Clean sheets and a big Lamar win

East Central’s girls defeated Pascagoula 7–0, while the boys finished in a scoreless draw. Neither East Central team conceded a goal in the reported Monday results.

Neshoba Central’s boys defeated Newton County 3–0, scoring twice before the break and once afterward. The girls played to a 0–0 draw, leaving Newton County scoreless in both matches.

Lamar’s boys reached double figures in a 10–2 home victory over Starkville Academy in Meridian.

Basketball: fast starts carry CCA boys and Simpson girls

Christian Collegiate Academy’s boys opened with a 21–4 first quarter against Woodlawn Prep, then outscored the visitors 23–5 in the second. The Bulldogs finished a 71–22 home win in Gulfport and moved to 1–0.

Simpson Academy’s girls took a 19–2 first-quarter lead at Wayne Academy and went on to win 60–23 in Waynesboro. The Cougars improved to 3–0.
